name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 3 January 1993 (English cryptic)

clue.text: Fix English downfall

blocks.note: ENG is the standard abbreviation for English
rain is a fall from the sky, read as down-fall

explanation.surface: A plea to stop England's slide, or a lament about English weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests ruin, but here it is weather falling from above.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrain something is to fix it deeply and firmly, as a habit or a dye is set in.

clue.text: Impetuosity shown in the landers

indicators.note: shown in says the letters are on display within the following words

blocks.note: spans the two words

explanation.surface: Boldness displayed by people coming ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and impetuous vigour, taken from French.

clue.text: Sign of health a newspaperman looks for

blocks.note: first meaning: blood flowing well through the body
second meaning: a paper selling plenty of copies

explanation.walkthrough: Circulation is both blood flow and the number of copies a paper sells.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthy blood flow marks a fit body, while strong sales are what every editor wants.

clue.text: Stone bearing name of relative on father's side

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the stone holds the next item inside it

blocks.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A gravestone carrying the name of a paternal relative.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a kinsman descended through the male line, from Latin for born in addition.

clue.text: Natural divinities observed in immature insects

blocks.note: first meaning: minor goddesses of woods, rivers and hills
second meaning: larval stages of dragonflies and similar insects

explanation.surface: Spirits of nature glimpsed in young bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these are nature spirits, and entomologists use the same word for insect young that hatch without a pupa.

clue.text: Happens to encounter risks

blocks.note: first meaning: occurs by luck, as in 'if he happens to call'
second meaning: takes a gamble, risks it

explanation.surface: Someone who stumbles into danger by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happens to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means both to occur by accident and to venture something risky.

clue.text: Unspiritual serviceman

blocks.note: first meaning: of the body, physical
second meaning: a junior army rank

explanation.walkthrough: The word is an adjective meaning bodily, and also a non-commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal punishment is bodily, the opposite of spiritual, and the rank sits above lance corporal.

clue.text: Pastoral car Diana crashed

indicators.note: crashed suggests a wreck, so the preceding letters are smashed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Diana smashed her car on a country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia was the idealised rural Greek region, so its adjective means rustic and idyllic.

clue.text: Beef most people have cold for example

blocks.note: what most people share is common
a beef is a grumble

explanation.surface: Most people eat their beef cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like meat, but it is slang for a grievance; complaint is also an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is a widespread ailment, and an ailment is called a complaint.

clue.text: Where one may dine on meat and hot water?

definitions.text: Where one may dine on meat and hot water?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one may dine on meat
blocks.note: surface reading: a restaurant serving meat
the setter's tease: a cooking or bathing image that the question mark marks as playful

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a restaurant specialising in grilled beef; the hot-water tag seems to be a playful extra the scan does not explain.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant whose menu centres on grilled cuts of beef is where diners go for meat.

clue.text: A party sailors have on deck

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
RN is the Royal Navy, the usual crossword source for sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors throwing a party on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like the ship's deck, but it is a verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room with flowers is to adorn or ornament it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Where doctor needs to care about decoration. That's comic!

indicators.note: about means around and turned over, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a common crossword doctor
the four letters of this word, rearranged
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
surface padding, an extra nudge: the town shares its name with a famous British comedian

explanation.surface: A doctor fussing over a medal, with a final punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: MORECAMBE is a seaside town in Lancashire, hence 'Where'; 'That's comic!' nods to Eric Morecambe, the British comedian of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Morecambe is a place name, so a question of location is answered by the town.

clue.text: Drink bird has in dish

blocks.note: Scotch whisky
a woodcock is a long-billed game bird

explanation.surface: A recipe where a bird is cooked in whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch woodcock is a British savoury of scrambled egg and anchovy on toast; it contains no bird at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The savoury is a named course on old British menus, so it is a dish in the culinary sense.

clue.text: Legitimate clue to eminent lawyer

blocks.note: legitimate means lawful
a light is an illuminating hint, as in throwing light on

explanation.surface: A lawful hint that points to a top barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminary of the courts is called a legal light, an idiom for a distinguished figure.

clue.text: Listener noting first gain by labour

indicators.note: first tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the ear is the organ that listens
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A music student's first progress through hard practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to obtain money or reward in return for work done.

clue.text: Italian artist trained as a comic

indicators.note: something trained is drilled into a new shape, so the following letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter who went to drama school to become a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Masaccio was a Florentine painter of the early Renaissance, famed for the Brancacci Chapel frescoes.

clue.text: They may aim to harm production

definitions.text: They may aim to harm production

blocks.note: surface reading: saboteurs or attackers with a target
setter's reading: workers who walk out to halt output

explanation.walkthrough: 'Aim' and 'harm' suggest attackers; the point is people who stop work.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who withdraw their labour deliberately stop factory output to press a demand.

clue.text: Coerces mounted soldiers

blocks.note: first meaning: forces someone into something
second meaning: cavalry troops

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense, to force, comes from the cavalry used to bully civilians.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pressed into something is to be forced, and historically mounted infantry bore the same name.

clue.text: True lady upset by unchastity

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the preceding letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A faithful wife distressed by infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual unfaithfulness in marriage, the commonest form of unchastity.

clue.text: Writer with French friends

blocks.note: first meaning: Kingsley or Martin, the British novelists
second meaning: the French word for friends

explanation.surface: An author who spends time with friends in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis wrote Lucky Jim, and in French the plural noun for male friends has the same spelling.

clue.text: They make for slower progress with snaps it is said

indicators.note: it is said tells us to go by how a word sounds spoken, not its spelling

blocks.note: snaps means splits apart, which has the same sound

explanation.surface: Photography slows a holiday drive down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snaps' suggests photos, but it means cracks in two.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices on a vehicle slow it, so they make movement slower.

clue.text: Long vehement harangue putting one in business

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the word that follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
trade is business

explanation.surface: A boss's long rant about bringing someone into the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is an angry, extended speech of denunciation.

clue.text: Principal object of editorial

blocks.note: principal means chief or leading
an article is an item or object

explanation.surface: A question about what an editorial is mainly for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as purpose, but it is a thing, an article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers the main opinion piece by the editor is called the leader or leading article.

clue.text: Bring up some obscure article

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Raising an obscure item in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' seems to mean mention; it means raise a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise or nurture them.

clue.text: It may help tourist to regulate volume

blocks.note: to guide is to steer or regulate
a volume is a book

explanation.surface: A gadget that lets a sightseer control the sound level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulate volume' suggests turning the sound down; volume is a book here.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel handbook of sights and routes is exactly what a visitor carries for help.

clue.text: Sotto voce remark — conflict of ideas

blocks.note: first meaning: a comment made in a low voice, out of others' hearing
second meaning, loosely

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a clear definition; the second only fits if read as two words, one side in a clash of views, and the scan may have garbled it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotto voce is Italian for under the breath, and an aside is a remark spoken that way.

clue.text: Model saints as Celtic heirs-elect?

indicators.note: to model is to shape anew, so the word that follows is remoulded into a fresh order

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car
the six letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Holy figures held up as exemplars for Celtic princes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' works twice: it gives the letter of Ford's car and tells us to reshape the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Among the old Irish and Scots, a tanist was the successor chosen in a chief's lifetime.

clue.text: Loud-mouth erects tent or part of it

indicators.note: part of it says the letters lie inside the run of words just before

blocks.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: A noisy camper putting up a tent, or just a section of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was the herald in the Iliad whose voice was as loud as fifty men, so his name means a loud-voiced person.
